A_target.statement:
Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a [[Definition:Decreasing Real Sequence|decreasing]] sequence with $a_n \to 0$.
Then $\displaystyle \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {-1}^{n + 1} a_n$ [[Definition:Convergent Series|converges]] to some $S$, and:
:$\size {S - S_N} \le a_{N + 1}$
where $S_N$ is the $N$th partial sum.

B_source.statement: Every [[Definition:Increasing Real Sequence|increasing]] real sequence which is [[Definition:Bounded Above Real Sequence|bounded above]] is [[Definition:Convergent Real Sequence|convergent]], and dually for decreasing sequences bounded below.

substitutions.a monotone bounded sequence: the even and the odd partial sums separately

derived.the common limit: the sum of the alternating series

object_map.reformulation: Split the oscillating partial sums into two monotone sequences squeezed against each other.

validity_conditions: The terms must decrease, so that even and odd partial sums are monotone.
The terms must tend to 0, so that the two monotone limits coincide.
proof_plan:
We have $S_{2 n + 2} - S_{2 n} = a_{2 n + 1} - a_{2 n + 2} \ge 0$ and $S_{2 n + 3} - S_{2 n + 1} = -a_{2 n + 2} + a_{2 n + 3} \le 0$.
So $\sequence {S_{2 n} }$ is increasing and $\sequence {S_{2 n + 1} }$ is decreasing.

By the [[Monotone Convergence Theorem (Real Analysis)|Monotone Convergence Theorem]], both subsequences converge.
As $S_{2 n + 1} - S_{2 n} = a_{2 n + 1} \to 0$, they have a common limit $S$, so the series converges.

$S$ lies between any two consecutive partial sums, so:
:$\size {S - S_N} \le \size {S_{N + 1} - S_N} = a_{N + 1}$
This is the [[Alternating Series Test]].
{{qed}}
